title: Async propagator fallback and sampling controller
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a resilient async propagation layer in SDKs and middleware that (1) preserves trace context across async/workers and dual-path transports, (2) provides deterministic fallback when upstream sampling headers are missing or truncated, and (3) exposes a central Sampling Controller for harmonizing sampling decisions across proxies and edge SDKs.

Scope:
- SDK middleware changes (Node/Python/Go) to attach deterministic trace tokens when W3C traceparent is absent or truncated.
- Lightweight in-process Sampling Controller library (stateless API) used by SDKs and edge proxies to reconcile sampling hints and apply rate-limited adaptive sampling.
- Fallback handshake protocol: short-lived provenance token + optional sticky-sampling header so downstream services can rehydrate the original sampling decision.
- Backwards compatibility: must interoperate with existing tracing backend and Otel-compatible collectors; header names prefixed to avoid collisions.
- Telemetry: add sampling decision events and fallback metrics to console (per-route sampled/unsampled counts, fallback-rate, header-truncation-rate).

Non-goals: global transaction-level tracing, deep changes to backend collectors, and any synchronous blocking APIs in edge SDKs.

Success criteria:
- End-to-end trace fidelity improves by >60% for async job/workers in internal e2e test harness (measured by % traces with consistent trace IDs and parent IDs).
- Fallback usage <1% for normal traffic but captured as a metric and sample traces for debugging.
- No more than 3% p95 latency increase in hot SDKs when the propagator is enabled (compare canary to baseline).

Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Async+Propagator+Fallback+Design
Design draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/designs/pull/1429
comments: 2026-02-16 - Initial scoping meeting with Observability, Edge, and SDK leads. Agreed to use a short provenance token (8 bytes hex) instead of full baggage to reduce header size. Action: Aisha to draft design doc.

2026-02-20 - Design doc posted (link above). Feedback from Edge team: avoid any on-path crypto HSM calls. Decided to sign tokens with HMAC keyed in config only for private deployments; hosted will use low-cost MAC with rotating keys. Follow-up: security review for hosted approach (ticketed).

2026-02-25 - Spike (ENG-38901) completed: measured header overhead across Node and Go SDKs; added microbenchmarks. Node p95 increased ~1.8% with optimistic async context restore; Go unaffected. Decision: implement non-blocking async hooks and leverage existing async-local-storage shims for Node.

2026-03-03 - Prototype PR opened for Node SDK: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/616. Early review from Daniel and Mei (Edge). Notes: rename header to "x-rwd-provenance" and add optional "x-rwd-sampling". Adjusted TTL of provenance token to 30s to cover typical worker handoffs.

2026-03-07 - QA run across canary routes (internal): observed fallback-rate 0.4% on bursty jobs; traced root cause to upstream NGinx truncation for headers >512 bytes. Mitigation: compact token + aggressive header trimming + server-side rewriter in edge proxy. TODO: add header-trim metric in Runtime.

2026-03-09 - Security review kickoff: discussed HMAC rotation and KMS integration for Private deployments. Outcome: document KMS integration pattern; mark feature optional behind enterprise flag for Private customers.

2026-03-10 - Planning: schedule SDK rollouts as follows - Node (canary 03/15), Go (canary 03/22), Python (canary 03/29). Observability OWNER: Priya Shah will add console widgets for fallback-rate and sampling-decision-breakdown.
next_steps: Finalize Node SDK PR feedback and merge canary, include telemetry counters (rwd.propagator.fallback.count, rwd.propagator.header_truncate.count)
Implement Sampling Controller API and publish lightweight npm/go/python packages
Add edge proxy header-rewrite rule to compact trace headers and avoid truncation on common routers
Create console dashboard: Observability > Traces > Propagator Health (fallback-rate, sampling-breakdown, per-route p95)
